targetText: the gens is an institution common to all barbarians until their entry into civilization and even afterwards... providing us at the same time with an unsuspected wealth of information about the fundamental features of social constitution in primitive times ; before the introduction of the state.
summary: The clan (gens) was the universal social structure of human societies before the rise of private property, class distinctions, and state authority.
context: Engels highlights Morgan's discovery that early Greek, Roman, Germanic, and Native American societies were all organized around egalitarian kinship clans. These clans managed public affairs democratically without standing armies, police, or kings.
